newsitem.title: USA: 'Empire' rules U.S. box office galaxy.
newsitem.headline: 'Empire' rules U.S. box office galaxy.

text.p: "The Empire Strikes Back" logged a second weekend as the main force in the box office galaxy, while gangster picture "Donnie Brasco" opened in second, according to studio estimates released on Sunday.

The reissue of the second movie in the "Star Wars" trilogy earned about $12.6 million over the Friday-to-Sunday period, taking its two-week total to $39.7 million. The movie's lifetime haul, since its release in 1980, is $262.4 million, which places it ninth on the all-time domestic gross list.
The movie, which is released by News Corp Ltd.'s 20th Century Fox, averaged $5,969 from an unchanged count of 2,111 screens.
"Donnie Brasco," which stars Al Pacino as a mobster and Johnny Depp as an undercover cop, earned $11.2 million. Its average of $7,452 from 1,503 screens was the highest in the top 10.
According to Sony Corp., which released the film, it opened better than recent mob genre films such as "Heat," "Casino" and "GoodFellas."
Slipping a notch to third was "Star Wars," with $7.0 million in its fifth weekend and a $2,957 average.
The reissue has earned $125.2 million, which takes the film's lifetime total to $447.9 million, topping the all-time domestic list.

The third movie in the trilogy, "Return of the Jedi," will be re-released on March 14. It was originally scheduled for release on March 7, but was delayed so as not to clash with radio humorist Howard Stern's well-reviewed "Private Parts."

Opening in fourth was Sony's "Booty Call," an urban-themed "double date from hell" romantic comedy that opened on Wednesday. Its three-day total of $6.4 million brings its cumulative gross to $8.0 million. It averaged $5,031 from 1,272 screens.

Fifth place went to the White House thriller "Absolute Power," which Clint Eastwood starred in, directed and produced. The movie earned $5.7 million over the weekend, bringing its three-week total to $36.8 million. It averaged $2,220 from 2,568 screens.
The movie is released by Sony, which handles four of the movies in the top 10 (including "Fools Rush In" at eighth) as well as "Jerry Maguire" at 11th.
The studio, which underwent a tumultuous time last year as executives were fired following poorly performing movies, claimed 40 percent of the weekend box office.
